explain.say: Many waterfalls form where a river flows from a band of hard rock onto softer rock. Seen from the side, it is like a layer cake of rock with water pouring over the top.

faq.q: Why does a waterfall need hard rock?
faq.a: Hard rock resists erosion, so it holds up the lip of the waterfall while softer rock below and downstream wears away faster. That difference makes the sudden drop.
Water undercuts the soft rock beneath the hard cap, leaving an overhang. When the overhang breaks off, the falls move upstream and leave a gorge behind them.
A deep pool at the foot of a waterfall, dug out by the force of falling water and the rocks it swirls around.
asks: Why is the water deep under a waterfall?

faq.q: What is the tallest waterfall in the world?
faq.a: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall on land, with a total drop of 979 metres and a single plunge of 807 metres.

faq.q: Can a waterfall form without hard and soft rock?
faq.a: Yes. Waterfalls also form where glaciers carved deep valleys and left side valleys hanging high above, or where faults or old lava flows make sudden steps in the land.

facts: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops 979 metres, the tallest uninterrupted waterfall on land.
Niagara Falls has moved about 11 kilometres upstream in roughly 12,000 years.
